about: Fake Spirit Halloween Costume mimics the cheap plastic costume bags sold at Spirit Halloween, the seasonal store chain: an orange packet with the grim-reaper Spirit logo, a big white panel where the product photo would be, and "Adult Size Costume, One Size Fits Most" in the corner. People drop a picture of an oddly specific person, moment or character into the white space and write a deadpan product title and an "Includes:" list. The joke is that anything, no matter how obscure or mundane, looks like it could be a real costume once it is sold in this packaging with a list of sad accessories.
origin: Spirit Halloween is a US chain of pop-up Halloween stores whose costume bags have a recognizable orange design. Edited packages with invented, oddly niche costumes became a recurring joke every autumn.
usage:
The template has five text boxes on the orange side. The first, larger box is the costume name: make it painfully specific, like "Guy Who Says 'Let's Circle Back'". The next four are the contents list; the second box usually reads "Includes:" and the last three are the items, each starting with a dash.

The items are where the jokes stack up: one real prop, one intangible thing ("- unearned confidence") and one letdown ("- nothing"). Paste or imagine a photo of the character in the white panel. Niche references to a specific job, fandom or family member land harder than famous characters, because the absurdity is that a store would sell it.
